findings.defective_text: Lines opening with an interrogative particle inside the mem triplet stand in exactly two verses (sweep: 2 verses: Lam.3.37, Lam.3.39): the first spliced at byte tier as מִ֣י זֶ֤ה אָמַר֙ וַתֶּ֔הִי אֲדֹנָ֖י לֹ֥א צִוָּֽה (oshb:Lam.3.37, byte tier; WEB “Who is he who says, and it comes to pass, when the Lord doesn’t command it?”, web:Lam.3.37), the second closing the triplet as “Why should a living man complain, a man for the punishment of his sins?” (web:Lam.3.39); the intervening verse opens מִפִּ֤י (oshb:Lam.3.38, byte tier) with no interrogative particle in the source, though its own WEB rendering poses a question.
findings.byte_evidence: oshb:Lam.3.37 opens מִ֣י (byte tier) - the interrogative the row does splice. oshb:Lam.3.39 opens מַה (byte tier) - the interrogative particle the row does NOT splice; for that second member the row offers only “Why should a living man complain, a man for the punishment of his sins?” (web:Lam.3.39), an English run whose only visible interrogative signal is its terminal question mark. The same sentence supplies the counterexample that disqualifies that evidence layer: oshb:Lam.3.38 opens מִפִּ֤י (byte tier), no interrogative particle, yet web:Lam.3.38 renders it “Doesn’t evil and good come out of the mouth of the Most High?” - a WEB question mark standing over a non-interrogative source line. Owner-ruled strategy §4: chapter/verse divisions, headings, WEB paragraphing/punctuation/capitalization NEVER drive or corroborate (E-23) - the bar covers corroboration, not driver work alone. MITIGATION, recorded honestly: the digit is byte-true (2 of the 3 mem-triplet verses do open on an interrogative particle), and the back seam is carried independently by the 1cp cohortative onset נַחְפְּשָׂ֤ה (oshb:Lam.3.40, byte tier), which this row's own rejected alternative names as the stronger voice-based seam over the rhetorical-question close; no span is at risk. Severity is scored from the counterfactual, not the outcome: had מַה not stood at 3:39, the census digit would have been wrong and unfalsifiable from the row's own evidence - the Isaiah shipped-HIGH failure shape.
findings.proposed_cure: Splice מַה (oshb:Lam.3.39, byte tier) beside the existing WEB rendering so the second member of the two-verse interrogative census rests on the source particle rather than on the translation's question mark.

coverage.not_confirmed_part: The sweep's zero is a zero of seven literal lexical classes and does not establish the absence of the defect. One barred instance stands in the corpus and the sweep is structurally unable to see it (P02-005), so its GREEN is a blind GREEN with respect to the corroboration arm of the binding rule. Read as a detector result, the null is sound; read as an assurance that no translation-layer artifact does work in a seam argument, it is not.
sweep_blind_spots: SCOPE MISMATCH (the primary blind spot): the sweep implements only the DRIVER half of E-23. Owner-ruled strategy §4 bars translation punctuation from driving OR corroborating; no class in the sweep tests corroboration, so a barred corroboration passes GREEN by construction. This is a rule/detector scope gap, not a vocabulary gap.

LEXICAL CLASS GAP (the operative cause of THIS null): the seven classes match only literal strings. 'interrogative', 'rhetorical question', 'poses a question' and 'why-question' are all invisible, because question_exclamation_driver matches only 'question mark' and 'exclamation mark|point'. Measured on this corpus: 14 question-family phrases, 0 flags.

The capitalization class matches only capitali[sz](e|ed|ation) and 'capital letter' - blind to 'capitalizes', 'capitalizing', 'capitals', 'uppercase' and 'initial capital'. It is correctly blind to the one 'capital' in this corpus (P01-001, 'the ruined capital', which is the city).
paragraph_layer requires the suffixes 'ing', ' break' or ' division' - blind to bare 'paragraph(s)', 'paragraph mark', 'paragraph boundary' and 'paragraph seam'.

No class exists at all for comma, colon, semicolon, dash/em dash, line break, indentation, italics or small caps - and none for 'verse division' or 'versification', which §4 bars in the same clause as punctuation.

english_sentence_layer needs 'WEB|English|translation' within 50 characters of 'sentence', so a bare 'sentence break' or 'sentence division' escapes; period_fullstop_driver's 'period' arm needs a boundary verb within 50 characters and will not cross a '.' or ';', so a two-sentence formulation escapes.

FIELD SCOPE: DRIVER_FIELDS is (boundary_rationale, strongest_rejected_alternative) only; device_notes and observed_substrate_signals are never read, though both carry seam-relevant corroboration here (P03-008's why-question of 5:20 sits in device_notes; P02-005 carries the device key voice.rhetorical_question_frame). TESTED, and honestly negative: re-running the shipped classes with the scope widened to all four fields still returns 0 flags, so field scope did NOT produce this null.

CURLY-QUOTE MASKING: every quoted WEB run is blanked before matching, so punctuation visible only INSIDE a quoted run is unreachable - which is exactly where the P02-005 question mark sits. TESTED, and honestly negative as a cause: with the mask disabled the shipped classes still return 0 flags on this corpus.

PARAPHRASE, conceded by the ledger itself ('paraphrased punctuation reliance is not fully mechanizable'; Machine-checkable: PARTIAL). The sweep is a lexical trigger, not a semantic test, which is why the ledger pairs it with a model audit lane; the Isaiah exemplar was caught by an audit, not by a sweep.

PRECISION, not recall: the (?<!Masoretic ) lookbehind exempts only that one exact adjacency, so 'the paragraphing of the Masoretic tradition' or 'MT paragraphing' would false-positive while a translation-layer claim written as 'Masoretic paragraphing' is silently exempted. Not exercised here (0 paragraph hits).
